title: Magnus effect
description: A spinning ball moving through air curves sideways, because its spin drags the air faster past one side than the other. It's why a sliced ball swerves, and it drove ships with tall spinning cylinders for sails.
effect: a spinning object moving through air is pushed sideways
pickWhy: A clear, named effect with real uses (rotor ships, curveballs, flettner rotors) and plenty still untried.
edbDesc: The phenomenon whereby a spinning object flying in a fluid creates a whirlpool of fluid around itself, and experiences a force perpendicular to the line of motion and away from the direction of spin. The overall behaviour is similar to that around an aerofoil with a circulation which is generated by the mechanical rotation, rather than by aerofoil action.
